thread:
maya: quick heads-up — opened PR to tighten the billing panel copy and drop a tiny SDK header example for quota reporting. still WIP but want eyes on the wording and the snippet.  

alex: linking the PR? i can skim in the next hour. curious what changed in the panel copy.

maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4521  — the big change is swapping 'tier' -> 'ingestion tier' in the usage table and clarifying that burst credits are applied per-minute not per-day. also added a short note about the grace window for quota checks.

sam: can you paste the SDK snippet here? easier to check inline.

maya: sure — kept it intentionally minimal. the idea is show headers + tiny backoff hint.

maya: ```python
# Python requests example
import requests
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage'
headers = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY',
  'X-Redwood-Client': 'docs-snippet/1.0',
  'X-Quota-Version': 'v2'  # new header to opt into fine-grained quota responses
}
resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code, resp.json())
```

jordan: looks fine. tiny nit — the header name `X-Quota-Version` might confuse folks who expect `X-Quota-Profile`. do we have a naming convention in the SDK guide?

maya: good call. i used `X-Quota-Version` to reflect the server-side contract we expect to evolve. if we rename i can add a short note in the migration section.

lia: also, if the panel text now says 'ingestion tier' we should update the dashboard label too — otherwise docs and UI diverge. who owns the dashboard panel copy?

alex: that would be eng-analytics. @sam can you ping them? i can include the dashboard link in the PR description so the change is traceable.

sam: pinged eng-analytics in #eng-metrics. added the dashboard URL and the exact string to change. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks. another thing — we added a short example about the quota grace window: 

maya: "When a client temporarily exceeds their quota due to burst credits, requests are allowed for up to 30s while metering catches up. After that, standard 429 behavior applies."

jordan: that sentence is good but let's be explicit about server clocks and clock skew. maybe 'up to 30s of allowed overage as measured by the service' so it's clear it's server-side.

maya: updated in the PR.

docs-bot: Automated check — docs lint: 1 warning (style/heading-case). Please address before merge.

maya: i'll fix the heading case and tighten one example.

alex: small ask — can we also surface an example of how to consume the quota response in JS and show the fields the server returns? helps support engineers.

maya: adding a tiny JS snippet now:

maya: ```js
// fetch example showing quota fields
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage', {
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`,
    'X-Quota-Version': 'v2'
  }
}).then(r => r.json()).then(j => {
  // server returns {remaining: 1200, window_seconds: 60, ingestion_tier: 'pro'}
  console.log('quota', j.remaining, j.ingestion_tier);
});
```

sam: neat. suggest we include a one-line note on how to handle 429s with exponential backoff and a short code pointer to the SDK helper.

maya: added a link to the SDK helper in the PR body and a 1-line backoff suggestion.

lia: after the lint fix and eng-analytics confirming the dashboard label, i'm good to approve.

alex: same. i'll do a quick pass on copy and approve.

maya: thanks all — will land after docs-bot is happy and eng-analytics confirms the dashboard change. planning to merge today.

sam: thx — can you drop a follow-up in #release-war-room when it's merged so support knows to expect the label change?

maya: will do.
